name: Russel E. Heacock's House, Monroe Street

documented_range.note: BUILT IN THE SPRING OF 1835, WHICH IS INSIDE THE SCENE YEAR AND BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Andreas: 'In the spring of 1835, he built a house on what he supposed was his lot, only to find that he was on Monroe Street, not Adams, whither he proceeded to remove it on rollers.' The house, its season, its owner and the fact that it was moved a block are all documented. The range opens on 1835-03-01 as the earliest reading of 'the spring'.

position.symbolic_location: South Division, local ENU E 465 N -615
position.note: OUTSIDE THE MODELLED GROUND, AND THE DATE OF THE MOVE IS UNKNOWN. Two things are invented here. First, WHICH STREET IT STOOD ON on 1 July 1835: Andreas gives no date for the removal, so the house may have been on Monroe or already on Adams. This record puts it on Monroe, where it was built, because that is the position the source actually states. Second, WHERE ON MONROE: nothing says. The northing is estimated from the plat module - the block pitch implied by the reconstruction recipes' Randolph-to-Washington bands, carried two blocks further south - and lands about 215 m beyond the southern edge of the e1834_harbor_cut heightfield, so the phase declares ground_contact: outside_modelled_ground. THE BUILDING IS IN THE DATASET AND NOT UNDER THE WALKER'S FEET until the terrain extends south.

derivation.reason: No source gives this building a lot. The placement is a frontage-band assignment tested for clearance and buildable ground, which is a production control and not a derivation from any line in the dataset.

footprint.note: PLACEHOLDER - NO DIMENSION IS ATTESTED. 22 x 30 ft is the schedule's D5 deep-plan frame cottage, sized for the largest documented household in the residents layer: a wife and five sons, the youngest born in this house. Every number is invented.

phases.change_note: The building as this dataset can state it on the scene date. Where the sources give a size, a plan or a fabric, the record carries it; where they do not, the note says so attribute by attribute.

ground_contact.note: Monroe Street lies about 215 m south of the southern edge of the e1834_harbor_cut heightfield (local N -400). There is no ground under any part of this building's outline, so whether it lands has no answer. The record is correct and the terrain has not reached it - the same state docs/LIBERTIES.md L40 recorded for two thirds of the town before the eastward extension.

function.note: THE ROLLERS ARE THE FINDING. A documented instance of a Chicago house being moved bodily one block in 1835 is evidence about construction, weight and the town's attitude to its own buildings, and it belongs to ROADMAP K4 as much as to K1. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE THIS RECORD: any date for the removal, which would settle which street the house stood on at the scene date; and a terrain epoch reaching south of Madison, which would put ground under it.
